question:
A prism of apex angle $A=60^{\circ}$ is used in the condition of minimum deviation. For this prism material in the visible region, the refractive index is approximated by

$$n(\lambda)=1.50+\frac{1.152\times10^{4}}{\lambda^2},$$

where $\lambda$ is in nm.

For a spectral line of wavelength $\lambda_1$, the measured minimum deviation is $\delta_{m1}=40^{\circ}$. For another nearby spectral line of wavelength $\lambda_2$, the measured minimum deviation is $\delta_{m2}=41^{\circ}$.

Use the minimum-deviation relation

$$n=\frac{\sin\left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)}.$$

(i) Determine the two wavelengths $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$.

(ii) Using $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, find the corresponding photon energy difference $\Delta E=|E_2-E_1|$ in eV. Use $hc=1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$.
